articles.title: Barcelona fight back from two goals down to beat Villarreal 3-2
articles.summary: Barcelona shook off a sloppy first half to beat Villarreal 3-2 in LaLiga on Sunday, coming back from two goals down against their opponents, who were reduced to 10 men. After a nightmarish start for Hansi Flick's side, a fading Villarreal could not cope with a persistent and fiery Barcelona in the second period. Barcelona remain top of the standings on 36 points, three ahead of Real Madrid after Jose Mourinho's side beat Celta Vigo on Saturday. Villarreal remain ninth on 15 points. Tajon Buchanan took just two touches to convert Fermin Lopez's lax giveaway into the opening goal for Villarreal after five minutes. Alberto Moleiro released Tani Oluwaseyi into space on the left flank and the Canadian international added Villarreal's second with a powerful finish two minutes later. Shops looted, streets ablaze as 'anti-system' riots rock Barcelona Even as Barcelona began to create chances, their game was plagued by errors, characterised by Lamine Yamal winning a penalty and then dragging it onto the post in the 23rd minute. Barcelona's comeback was finally ignited by Gerard Martin, who headed in a quickly taken short corner in the 57th minute. Fermin Lopez finished a brilliant move to level the score in the 61st minute. Centre-forward Raphinha had sprinted to the right-back spot to thwart a counter-attack and was involved again in a sequence that finished with Lamine Yamal finding Fermin on the left side of Villarreal's box. With Barcelona hungry for a third, what seemed like a mountainous task was completed in a matter of 10 minutes. Lamine Yamal's cross from the right was turned across the line by Villarreal defender Pau Navarro inside his own six-yard box. Navarro was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow as Barcelona saw out the victory.

articles.title: 2 persons go missing after being swept away by Kaup Beach in Karnataka's Udupi
articles.summary: Udupi: Two persons, including a 15-year-old boy, went missing after being swept away by strong waves while swimming at Kaup beach on Sunday evening. Another teenager was rescued and admitted to a hospital in Udupi . The missing persons have been identified as Sameer (20), son of Ziaulla from Shivamogga, and Malik Riyan (15) from Davanagere. Mohammed Isaq (15), who was rescued, is undergoing treatment at a hospital in Udupi. Ziaulla and 11 members of his family had come to Udupi on a visit. His elder son, Mohammed Jafar (20), is pursuing engineering in Kundapura taluk. Jafar and his friend had brought the family to Kaup beach for an outing. While five youngsters from the group entered the sea for a swim, the remaining family members, including women, stayed on the shore. Lifeguards reportedly warned the youngsters against entering the sea due to the danger. However, they allegedly moved a few metres further into the water, away from the lifeguards' watch and continued swimming. Two farmers drown in Hemavathi backwaters in Karnataka's Hassan taluk Sameer, Riyan and Isaq were caught in the waves and swept away. On hearing the cries of people on the beach, boat operators and lifeguards rushed to the spot and managed to rescue all three. The rescued boys were given first aid, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), before being shifted to the hospital by ambulance, police said. However, Sameer and Riyan remain missing. A team led by diver Eshwar Malpe arrived at the spot to assist in the search operation. A search is underway, but no trace of the missing youngsters. Kaup police visited the spot, registered a case and are investigating.

articles.title: David Beckham hails Madhya Pradesh tribal teen who stopped her marriage
articles.summary: Bhopal: Former England football captain and UNICEF goodwill ambassador David Beckham has praised a 17-year-old tribal girl from Madhya Pradesh 's Jhabua district for standing up against her marriage and securing her right to continue education. Beckham shared the story of Heema Ninama, who belongs to the Bhil community, on his Instagram account on November 20, World Children's Day, praising her courage and determination. Heema's story, shared by one of Britain's most celebrated footballers, highlights how timely support and opportunities empower girls to make important decisions about their lives. Beckham said his 20 years of association with UNICEF showed him that girls could lead, progress and make crucial decisions about their lives when they received proper support. He highlighted how Heema stopped her child marriage with the help of her teachers and now aspires to shape the future of other girls. Beckham also praised UNICEF and its partner organisations for their efforts to protect children's rights. He called for continued collective efforts to provide children and adolescent girls with opportunities to progress. Bengaluru: 120 waste pickers turn community leaders; fight violence, child marriage Pre-wedding photoshoot exposes child marriage plan in Maharashtra; minor rescued The football star's endorsement also brings back memories of the 2002 sports comedy-drama 'Bend It Like Beckham'. The film revolves around Jess Bhamra, an 18-year-old girl who dreams of playing football like her idol, Beckham, rather than following the traditional expectations of her family. UNICEF India has also shared Heema's story through a short documentary highlighting her courage and determination, a state official said. A UNICEF team visited Jhabua and documented her journey at her school and village. Heema also takes an active part in sports alongside her studies. Heema, a resident of Barkheda village in Jhabua district, opposed her marriage while studying in Class 11. Her family had arranged her marriage at an early age, but she wanted to continue her studies. She refused to marry and sought help from her schoolteachers, officials said. The principal of Sandipani School in Kalyanpura, G P Ojha, and other teachers counselled her family about the harmful consequences of child marriage and the importance of girls' education. Their intervention, along with Heema's determination, stopped the marriage. She continued her studies and passed her Class 11 examination in first division. She is currently studying in Class 12, officials said. Heema aspires to become a teacher and help other girls pursue education and become self-reliant. MP Women and Child Development Minister Nirmala Bhuria, in a statement issued on Sunday evening, praised Heema's courage and said the Madhya Pradesh government is committed to ending the social practice of child marriage. She said the government was focusing on effectively implementing the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, and strictly enforcing its provisions. The government is also creating awareness among girls about their rights, education and future, she added. "Our objective is not merely to prevent child marriages but also to create an environment where every girl can complete her education without fear and make her own life decisions," Bhuria said. She said the Women and Child Development Department was conducting awareness programmes through anganwadi centres, schools, communities and local institutions. The programmes inform girls about the consequences of child marriage, the importance of education and their legal rights. The department also sensitises parents, she added. Under the law, the minimum marriage age is 18 years for women and 21 years for men. The Act prescribes punishment of up to two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh for specified offences.

articles.title: MotoGP maestro Marquez wins record eighth premier class title in Portugal
articles.summary: Ducati's Marc Marquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP crown at the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday, his eighth-place finish enough to establish an unassailable lead in the standings and place him alongside the great Giacomo Agostini on eight premier-class titles. Marquez needed to finish in the top nine in Sunday's race and despite starting second on the grid, the Spaniard rode with caution to finish eighth and seal the title with a round to spare. The race was won by Marco Bezzecchi, who held a 102-point advantage over Marquez at one stage this season, while his Aprilia team mate Jorge Martin and Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez completed the podium. However, all eyes were on Marquez, who marked the occasion by scaling a scaffold to address the cheering fans before watching a big-screen montage of the defining moments of his career. MARQUEZ, THE 'GOAT' As a final flourish, the Spaniard ascended a staircase accompanied by the silhouette of a goat on the screen, a nod to his growing 'Greatest of All Time' status, before receiving a golden commemorative helmet from Agostini himself. He then attached another plaque with his name engraved on it on the Tower of Champions before embracing and lifting it over his head. "We need to be happy. I know that we are here celebrating a historic moment. I know how I suffered," said an emotional Marquez, who underwent double surgery midway through the season. "I know that in the middle of the season, the fans believed more than I did. My people believed more than I did. But I kept pushing, I kept doing my best. "I said last year that it was a championship where I was at peace with myself. This one is for all the fans that believed in me from 2020 until now. So thanks to all of you, this is for all of you." Bezzecchi fires first salvo by winning Thailand MotoGP as Marquez retires Marquez came agonisingly close to securing the title in Saturday's sprint but his hopes were dashed when he crashed out on the penultimate lap while running in third place, a finish that would have been sufficient to crown him champion. But unlike Saturday's overcast conditions and spots of rain on the circuit, Sunday's 25-lap race was held in bright sunshine. TOP-NINE FINISH ENOUGH FOR MARQUEZ Martin needed to outscore Marquez by 18 points while the Ducati rider's equation was far more simple: secure a top-nine finish regardless of his rivals' results to get his hands on the trophy. Marquez had been cautious in the sprint but this time he shot off the line to take the lead from polesitter Bezzecchi while several riders jostled for position behind him, with Martin moving up from seventh to fourth. But Marquez was soon swallowed up by the faster Aprilia bikes around him, with the championship leader quickly falling to seventh as he exercised caution amid aggressive overtaking. A crash from Pedro Acosta moved Marquez up to sixth but he had to concede two places to Fabio Di Giannantonio and Ai Ogura, with the Ducati rider happy to open the door to let them pass knowing eighth would be good enough for the title. Up front, Bezzecchi finally moved past Fernandez to take the lead on lap 15 while Martin also found a way past three laps later with an identical overtake to make it a factory Aprilia one-two. On lap 19, Marquez fell to ninth as KTM's Brad Binder nudged him aside to overtake and there was concern from his legion of fans at the Algarve International Circuit, but a crash from Diogo Moreira on the last lap moved Marquez up to eighth. "Super happy about the season, obviously some highs and some lows, but my best season in MotoGP so far," said Bezzecchi, who missed races with his own injuries. "Still a lot of things to improve. But congrats to Marc, he really deserves everything. He's one of the strongest riders in history, so to fight with him is an honour. "Hopefully next year I will fight again and make his life even harder."

articles.title: 50 crore people lifted out of poverty, but some still hesitant to acknowledge it: PM Modi
articles.summary: Ahmedabad: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said some individuals still hesitate to acknowledge that 50 crore people have been pulled out of poverty in the country, in an apparent dig at the Opposition. Addressing BJP workers virtually during a post-Diwali ‘Sneh Milan’ programme organised across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat, he said the achievement reflected the success of his government’s policies and efforts. VIDEO | Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, during a virtual address to Gujarat BJP workers, says, "For the first time after 1,000 years of slavery, 50 crore people have come out of poverty. Some people hesitate to acknowledge this." (Source: PM Modi YT) (Full video available… pic.twitter.com/AHfs6SlVvQ — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) November 22, 2026 “All those who sacrificed their lives for independence, all those who dedicated their lives to freedom, all those who spent their youth in jails for independence, wherever their souls may be, today they must be the happiest seeing this World Bank report, thinking, ‘finally, poverty is leaving my country’,” he said. Government not bothered about health of economy but about Rahul Gandhi speaking about it: Congress According to a World Bank report, India’s extreme poverty rate dropped sharply to 2.6 per cent in 2023 from 27.1 per cent in 2011, with the country lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty. “A thousand years of slavery had impoverished us; for the first time after a thousand years of slavery, 50 crore people are coming out of poverty. There can be no greater satisfaction in life than this, no greater achievement than this,” Modi said. However, he said, some people were still reluctant to acknowledge the achievement. “I know many people still hesitate to say this aloud, because all of this happened during this period (BJP rule). They don’t like it. Whether they like it or not, we have the satisfaction that our efforts have borne fruit,” Modi said. Terming the development the beginning of a new chapter in the lives of citizens, he said coming generations would witness the country’s “golden era”. “Our intention is true, our policy is right, our direction is right, and there is no shortcoming in our hard work,” he said. The BJP had organised the programme across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat. Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel listened to the PM's virtual address in his Ghatlodia constituency. Modi said this year’s Diwali was significant for him as it marked 25 years since he became Gujarat’s CM in October 2001. He credited generations of BJP workers for supporting him in his political journey and said their hard work had enabled him to serve his home state and the country. Recalling the devastating 2001 Gujarat earthquake, Modi said his first Diwali as chief minister was spent with affected families. “That day, my belief became very strong that the true happiness of festivals, the true joy of festivals, lies in lighting a lamp of hope in someone else’s life,” he said. Modi said the spirit of public participation had helped Gujarat overcome the devastation and transform Kutch into a new centre of hope. The reconstruction efforts subsequently spread across the state, leading to a wider transformation, he said. Recalling Gujarat’s development journey, Modi said the state, once largely associated with trade, had expanded its presence in sectors such as agriculture, dairy, industries, semiconductors, petrochemicals, automobiles and green energy. He said Gujarat’s economic progress had contributed significantly to the country’s development and reiterated his earlier slogan of achieving national development through Gujarat's development. Recalling the difficult years around 2001, he said party workers had gone door-to-door collecting ‘sukhdi’ (a traditional sweet) for poor families to provide them with essential nutrition. They had also arranged cattle fodder from different parts of the country during droughts and organised cattle camps, he said. 'Acting like frustrated cat': Kangana Ranaut slams Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Indian economy The PM said public participation had helped Gujarat overcome droughts and water shortages. “Campaigns to conserve water and construct check dams had gradually turned into mass movements, changing the situation in the state,” he said. The prime minister also referred to the Garib Kalyan Melas launched during his tenure as the CM in 2001, saying they helped build confidence among poor families and encouraged them to come out of poverty. “The experience gained from launching such programmes helped me create welfare schemes introduced by my government at the Centre after 2014,” said the PM. Modi recalled that when his government started opening bank accounts for the poor, critics questioned their utility, while similar doubts were raised over the provision of LPG connections to households that could not afford cylinder refills. “We kept making scheme after scheme and taking them to the last person in the queue. We proved what social justice means for those who are rightful claimants and in need. And who were the ones without bank accounts? Our Dalit families, tribal families, the oppressed and downtrodden, as well as the women,” the PM said. While bank accounts were opened, gas stoves arrived in homes, and electricity connections and Ayushman cards were distributed to the needy, he said. “As a result of all these schemes, 50 crore people have come out of poverty,” the PM added. Modi urged BJP workers to keep national interest above party interests. He said the social harmony and unity developed in Gujarat would help the state and the country progress. He expressed confidence that Gujarat would achieve much more in the next 20 years than it had accomplished over the previous 25 years.

articles.title: 'Criticise decisions, not constitutional institutions': CJI Surya Kant
articles.summary: Shimla: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday said that citizens in a democracy have the right to criticise the decisions of constitutional bodies but should avoid targeting the institutions themselves. Interacting with students on the sidelines of the 10th convocation of the Central University of Himachal Pradesh (CUHP) at Dharamshala, where he was the chief guest, the Chief Justice observed that people often fail to distinguish between a decision and the institution behind it. According to him, this tendency risks undermining public confidence in institutions essential to sustaining democracy, a university statement said. While citizens in a democracy have the right to criticise the decisions of constitutional bodies, they should avoid targeting the institutions themselves, he said. SCBA seeks contempt action against lawyer for sharp personal remarks against CJI Surya Kant In his convocation address on Sunday, Justice Surya Kant drew on the Himalayan landscape around him to urge the graduating students to be patient in pursuing their goals, reminding them that the road to any destination in the mountains is seldom straight and that no one climbs a mountain alone. The convocation was held at the auditorium of Government Degree College, Dharamshala. Degrees were conferred on 702 students and 32 gold medals were presented, 23 of them to women. The 702 graduates included 584 postgraduates, 29 undergraduates and 48 PhD scholars, besides diploma holders. The university newsletter and five books by faculty members were released on the occasion. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu told the students that a degree is not only recognition of a student's hard work but also represents their responsibility towards society and the nation. Emphasising that any country's greatest strength lies in its educated, aware and responsible citizens, he said education is not merely about securing employment; it is a means of developing critical thinking, understanding, research, innovation and bringing positive changes to society. In an era of rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, data science and digital technology, the education system must prepare young people not only to seek employment but also to generate employment, undertake research and promote innovation, he was quoted as saying in the statement. 50 years of 42nd Amendment to Constitution: How 'secular and 'socialist' survived Governor Kavinder Gupta called upon the university to work towards emerging as a centre of impactful research on Himalayan challenges, including climate change, disaster management, water conservation, biodiversity and rural development, stressing that universities must connect academic excellence with the needs of society. "Knowledge empowers us, values give us direction and determination enables us to achieve our goals. Your degree may earn you recognition, but your character and values will earn you lasting respect," he said, urging students to remain committed to integrity, humility and lifelong learning. Highlighting the ecological and cultural significance of the Himalayas, the Governor said development must be pursued in harmony with nature. He urged the university to promote focused research on Himalayan ecology, disaster preparedness, water resources, tribal communities, natural farming and tourism, so that academic pursuits contribute to sustainable development in the region. Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court, Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia, and Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri were among those who attended the ceremony. The Vice Chancellor of the university, Sat Prakash Bansal, said the university's vision was 'local to global'. He highlighted its debut in the 701-800 band of the Times Higher Education World University Rankings and its 239th place in Southern Asia in the QS Asia University Rankings, and said its h-index had risen from 22 to 86 and its patents from one to 70.

articles.title: 'CJP is here to unite India': Abhijeet Dipke accuses govt of fuelling religious divisions
articles.summary: Panaji: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) convenor Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday alleged that the government is fostering religious divisions to divert attention from real issues affecting the common people and slammed the “poaching” of elected leaders and "vote theft". He appealed to citizens across the country to rise above religious and caste identities and focus on issues affecting their daily lives. Addressing a gathering in Panaji in the presence of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, Dipke said CJP was committed to bringing people together and reclaiming India's social fabric, which he said was rooted in the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and B R Ambedkar. "Citizens should always maintain their ability to think as citizens. When they take away that ability and force you to think as a Hindu, Muslim or Christian, you stop focusing on the real issues that affect your daily livelihood. You stop questioning the government, which is responsible for those issues," he said. Alleging that people were being divided along religious and caste lines to help political parties remain in power, Dipke said CJP wanted to unite citizens irrespective of their religion, caste, creed or political ideologies. "CJP is here to unite India. CJP is here to reclaim the very social fabric of India, which was based on the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar," he added. The CJP founder also questioned what he described as the "erosion of democratic principles", referring to the political developments in Goa in 2017, when several Congress MLAs joined the BJP after the Assembly elections. "Today, everybody is talking about vote theft. In Goa, they stole MLAs. It started with the stealing of MLAs in Goa, which has now led to the issue of vote theft," he alleged. Questioning the Constitutional propriety of such political developments, Dipke said those accusing CJP of being unconstitutional should explain how elected representatives switching parties to help form governments could be justified. "We are not here to get into power. We are not here to make any party win. What we really want to achieve is an India where Hindus, Muslims and Christians live together and everybody can practise their faith without any discrimination," he added. While outlining the CJP's national objectives, Dipke also raised concerns over land ownership, environmental degradation and development projects in Goa. Abhijeet Dipke alleges attack on villagers opposing mega housing project in Goa's Karapur-Sarvan He alleged that politicians and builders were working together to take over land belonging to local communities, saying land acquisition and large-scale construction could eventually threaten Goa's traditions, culture, and identity. Referring to a proposed 130-acre township project in Karapur, he questioned the priority being given to luxury developments over essential infrastructure such as schools, colleges and hospitals. Dipke also raised concerns over water scarcity in the area, alleging that the project could put additional pressure on groundwater resources. He demanded that Section 39A be scrapped, claiming that it threatened the land rights of Goans. He appealed to civil society groups and members of the legal fraternity to join the campaign against the provision. Section 39A of the Goa Town and Country Planning (TCP) Act empowers the Chief Town Planner to modify land-use zoning on specific plots following a notification and public objection window. "Goan youth are not receiving an adequate share of the benefits generated by the state's tourism industry. Local youth should be given priority in tourism-related businesses and employment," Dipke said. Recalling the solidarity shown by people in Goa during protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, Dipke said citizens should stand up against injustice even when the affected people were strangers to them.

articles.title: India administers 1 crore HPV vaccine doses to 87% eligible girls
articles.summary: Within nine months of the launch, India has administered one crore doses of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign. The achievement is an important milestone towards protecting adolescent girls against HPV infections that can potentially cause cervical cancer. The nationwide campaign provides free, safe, and voluntary single-dose HPV vaccines, with consent, to a targeted group of 14-year-old girls. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare stated that they have covered nearly 87 per cent of the targeted 1.2 crore girls based on the Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 population estimates. According to the department, six states: Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar, successfully achieved 100 per cent of their target populations under the campaign. Meanwhile, Assam recorded 95.63 per cent coverage, followed by Telangana (95.28 per cent), Karnataka (93.16 per cent), and Uttarakhand (90.17 per cent). Two states, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan, crossed the 80 per cent coverage mark with 86.21 per cent and 85.23 per cent, respectively. Kerala (77.02 per cent), Tamil Nadu (76.12 per cent), Odisha (74.9 per cent), and Dadra and Nagar Haveli (72.9 per cent) crossed the 70 per cent mark. India’s HPV vaccine Cervavac receives WHO’s safety nod for global distribution In terms of absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh 14-year-old girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with 13.7 lakh and Gujarat with 7.75 lakh girls. Besides focusing on expanding coverage, the campaign has also placed emphasis on parental awareness and credible knowledge about HPV vaccination with the help of school teachers, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs) and other frontline healthcare workers. Digital health infrastructure has been an important enabler of the nationwide campaign, with the U-WIN platform supporting real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking and digital vaccination records. Programme managers are using the platform to monitor vaccination progress at the district level, identify coverage gaps and eligible girls yet to be vaccinated, and support more effective planning and resource allocation. The platform also enables parents to book HPV vaccination slots for their daughters and download digital vaccination certificates, making the vaccination process more accessible, convenient and transparent.​ Cervical cancer remains a significant public health concern and an important cause of cancer-related illness and mortality among women. Persistent infection with certain high-risk types of HPV is responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancer cases. The HPV vaccination is among the most effective preventive interventions available to reduce the risk of infections that can turn fatal.

articles.title: Spent three years on 'Ramayana' music, turned down 10-12 films: A R Rahman
articles.summary: Panaji: Oscar-winning composer A R Rahman on Sunday said he devoted nearly three years to the music of “Ramayana” and had to turn down 10 to 12 film projects to immerse himself in the world of the mythological epic. Rahman, who has composed the Ranbir Kapoor -starrer's music in collaboration with renowned German composer Hans Zimmer, said some compositions went through more than a dozen versions before being finalised. "We've been doing ‘Ramayana’ music for three years, the themes and everything. And some of them have like, 12-13 versions. The ‘Ravana Tandav’ actually had 12-13 versions and then we finally found a version which everybody liked,” Rahman said. “The process was beautiful. Because of ‘Ramayana’, I left almost 10-12 movies, just to be in the zone. Many, many important big filmmakers I left. And I’m proud of it,” he added. 'Ramayana' crosses Rs 1000 crore at domestic box office Rahman was speaking at a press conference following the screening of filmmaker Bharat Bala’s “Banaras” at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) here. The music of “Ramayana” has generated considerable discussion among listeners with songs like “Ravana Tandav” and “Mangal Rang” receiving both praise and criticism. Asked about his approach to choosing projects despite a demanding schedule, Rahman said he takes up assignments only when he feels a strong connection with them. “I think I enjoy it. I only accept when I really love a project and I enjoy it, it nourishes my artistic sense and my whole team gets excited,” he said. The composer also spoke about the challenge of bringing together traditional Indian music and contemporary global sounds. “It is terrifying but we have to do it because I love both. I am multicultural in a way,” he said. “When I was doing traditional music, playing for other people traditionally, I was listening to modern music. So my mindset has got a modern thing and I compartmentalise both. Sometimes I get confused,” he added. “Ramayana”, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic. The first instalment features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. “Banaras”, which had its premiere at IFFI, is a Hindi drama set against the backdrop of Hindustani classical music and the cultural landscape of Varanasi. The film stars Neeraj Kabi, Shahana Goswami and Abhishek Banerjee, alongside Chhaya Kadam. Rahman has composed the music and also serves as an executive producer. "This film was a great opportunity. Not every time does a filmmaker come with a musical subject, where the lead singer is singing a song based on a musical family and original music. It's not something that they compose, but something that I compose for them. So I felt like I grabbed the opportunity," he said about the film. As a musician, Rahman said he likes to bring together influences from cultures that might appear geographically distant. "There is this constant seeking in me, where I enjoy exploring every culture, starting with the South Indian cultures of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, as well as Punjab, Bengal and Maharashtra. Each one of them has a distinct identity," he said. A R Rahman scripts history as first Indian musician to win Golden Plate Award "Sometimes I mix them up because I think that in India, we are one. Even though we have different cultures, it's nice to bring them together," he added. Giving the example of the popular "Dil Se" song "Jiya Jale", which features Malayalam lyrics, and the music of Imtiaz Ali's "Amar Singh Chamkila", Rahman said languages carry their own musical character and influence the way he approaches a composition. "With 'Amar Singh Chamkila', it was Punjab. I am from South India, while Punjab is in the north, but listening to Punjabi songs inspired me. While researching, I realised that the language itself has a certain potency, a certain power when the songs are sung. Bengali, on the other hand, has a certain softness about it," he said. articles.title: Spurious cosmetic products under lens in Keralam after users suffer serious health issues
articles.summary: Thiruvananthapuram: With the use of cosmetic products containing excessive mercury content causing serious health issues to a couple of persons in Keralam, the state government has decided to step up vigil against such products. Two persons, including a 17 year old girl and a known 'Mapilapattu' (traditional folk song of Muslim community) singer, have come out in the open after suffering serious kidney ailments due to excessive mercury content in skin-lightening creams purchased online. While the 17 year old girl from Malappuram was influenced by social media promotions of the cream by influencers, singer Salim Kodathoor used a cream suggested by a friend. Both of them are under treatment for kidney ailments that leads to loss of protein. Keralam: Singer Saleem Kodathoor claims he suffered kidney disease due to fairness cream use A couple of months back the state Drugs Control Authority had seized even Pakistan made spurious cosmetic creams in a state wide raid carried out following reports of spurious cosmetic products causing health hazards. Spurious cosmetic products worth around Rs 9.64 lakh were then seized. While the permissible mercury level is one part per million (ppm), spurious products with up to 20,000 ppm were among those seized. articles.title: UP assembly polls 2027: BJP pins hopes on law-order, cultural nationalism; drafts 'Triple S' mission
articles.summary: New Delhi: The ruling BJP will fight the upcoming Uttar Pradesh polls primarily on law and order, women's safety and development planks, with a robust outreach to beneficiaries of its "life-changing" schemes, besides keeping cultural nationalism and ideological issues firmly in play, party sources have indicated. While the party intends to draw a sharp contrast with the previous Samajwadi Party government on governance, the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) will also figure as a key poll issue, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah recently asserting that the BJP will implement it in Uttar Pradesh if it gets a mandate for a third consecutive term in assembly elections early next year. On the opposition's attempt to highlight alleged shortcomings of the ten-year rule and particularly the "Ram Mandir chanda chori" charge, the BJP intends an aggressive ideological counter, sources indicated. Law and order, women's safety and the 'labharthi' network will be at the heart of our campaign." The same source told PTI that the party has prepared a "Triple S" formula -- 'Sangathan, Sarkar and Sahyogi dal' -- under its “Mission-2027” blueprint. According to sources, party strategists have planned intensive "labharthi sampark", voter-list campaigns backed by digital monitoring and a sustained narrative on the Yogi government's crime control record. Targeted programmes are being organised among youth, women, farmers and Dalit communities, while senior leaders will reinforce the good-governance model through rallies and local meetings. articles.summary: Panaji: India has seen the number of international film productions coming to the country increase from 25 to 30 annually to more than 150 to 200, said Prithul Kumar, Joint Secretary (Films), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, during a session on India Cine Hub. The government's single-window digital platform, initially designed to assist international productions and co-productions with film visas and shooting permissions, has since expanded to integrate state governments and departments such as the Railways and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) , allowing filmmakers to access multiple permissions through a single portal. The initiative, Kumar said, aims to reduce the time and effort filmmakers spend navigating administrative processes, allowing them to focus on filmmaking instead. 'Michael is magic': Anupam Kher praises Michael Jackson biopic, calls Jaafar Jackson 'outstanding' Kumar was speaking at a panel discussion at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) . The discussion, titled ‘Filming Made Easy: India’s Rise as a Global Filming and Production Hub’, also featured actor-director Anupam Kher and Grainne Brunsdon, director at Screen Australia. It was moderated by film critic and journalist Rajeev Masand. Anupam Kher said the process of obtaining shooting permissions had become considerably easier over the years. Recalling his experience directing ‘Tanvi The Great’, he said, “It was a cakewalk. You go to a portal and get things done.” He also recalled how filmmakers earlier had to pay bribes to the police and municipal authorities to facilitate shoots. “Sometimes, this happened even during shoots. I don't think that's happening anymore,” he said. Anupam, who has worked in the film industry for over four decades, said the country's geographical and cultural diversity continued to make it an attractive destination for international productions. Citing films such as Payal Kapadia's ‘All We Imagine as Light’ and Aamir Bashir’s ‘The Winter Within’ as examples of productions that benefited from India Cine Hub, Kumar said the platform was continuing to expand its reach. The platform also facilitates international co-productions. Brunsdon said the first official co-production between India and Australia had been approved under the bilateral treaty. The film, which was shot entirely in India, is currently in post-production. She said the diversity of Indian locations, the skills of its filmmakers and their connection with audiences made the country an attractive co-production partner. Screen Australia had brought 12 producers to Film Bazaar to explore collaborations with Indian filmmakers and producers. Kumar said the platform was working towards integrating more services, including drone permissions, which currently come through the Digital Sky platform. He added that the ministry was also working on simplifying the documentation required for film visas. However, Anupam cautioned against middlemen exploiting the system by offering to secure permissions on behalf of filmmakers for a fee. “Filmmakers should use the portal directly rather than relying on intermediaries,” he said. NFDC India to launch digital collectible project at IFFI 2023 The discussion also brought up the financial uncertainties filmmakers face while scouting locations. A filmmaker from Bengaluru pointed out that unpredictable charges for shooting at public locations could force directors to alter their creative plans. The panel discussion concluded with Masand recalling an interview with Tom Cruise in Paris a few years ago. He said he had pointed out that two of the actor's films were set in Mumbai and Kashmir but were shot in Abu Dhabi and Canada. “I told him, you owe us to come and shoot in our country,” Masand recalled. Cruise, he said, responded that he would love to shoot in India but that the permission process needed to become easier. “Sitting here today, I feel like that could be a reality,” Masand added. The International Film Festival of India is on till November 28 in multiple locations across Goa including Panaji, Margao, Porvorim and Ponda.

CCPA slaps Rs 10 lakh fine on firm for advertising 'anti-drone gun' on IndiaMART
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of Rs 10 lakh on AirOne Robotics Pvt Ltd for listing and advertising an “Anti-drone gun VKSP03-PRO” on the e-commerce platform IndiaMART without mandatory disclosures and the required regulatory authorisations. In its order, CCPA Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and engaging in unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The authority noted that the company maintained an active commercial listing on a prominent marketplace, which carried full technical specifications, a price tag of Rs 8,30,000 and an “In stock” indicator. The CCPA said this clearly established an intent to offer the product for sale and solicit prospective buyers. AirOne Robotics had claimed that the product was a “non-active/inert replica”. The regulator rejected the explanation, describing it as “a bare assertion, made only after the Show Cause Notice and contradicted by the listing itself”. It further observed that the firm's successive versions of its defence were inconsistent with one another. The company also argued that terms such as “Anti-drone gun”, “electronic warfare device” and “neutralising drones” were used purely as descriptive titles to convey the aesthetic design of a conceptual and ornamental model. The CCPA dismissed this contention as well. The regulator emphasised that whether actual sales took place or whether the product was subsequently claimed to be an inert dummy did not reduce the advertiser's culpability. CCPA imposes penalties on 41 restaurants for levying service charges without customer's consent Hosting and advertising restricted electronic warfare equipment without statutory authorisations and mandatory disclosures prohibiting civilian use, as required under the Cabinet Secretariat's jammer guidelines and telecom laws, amounted to a deceptive advertisement and an unfair trade practice, it held. AirOne Robotics has been directed to ensure that all future advertisements and listings comply with the Consumer Protection Act and do not carry false or misleading claims regarding the operational capabilities, availability or lawful use of such equipment. The company must submit a compliance report within 15 days of the order. Incorporated in March 2026 and registered in Howrah, West Bengal, AirOne Robotics is engaged in the manufacture and wholesale trade of machinery and equipment, engineering and technical consultancy, and the production of radar equipment, GPS devices, and search, detection and navigation equipment. Anti-drone guns are wireless transmitting or jamming devices designed to interfere with licensed GPS and radio frequency spectrum. They fall under the category of restricted radio communication equipment regulated under various laws. The CCPA had earlier issued an advisory on April 29, 2022, cautioning against the illegal facilitation and sale of wireless jammers on e-commerce platforms.
